question_text: Draw a dedicated Current Sense Amplifier (CSA) configured for current sensing. What makes it unique, and what are its pros and cons?
answer_text:
Pros: A unique floating input stage allows V_CM to be much greater than V_s with large input impedance. A precision integrated gain network maximizes accuracy and minimizes drift.
Cons: Usually only offered at fixed gains, and greater accuracy is achieved at higher currents.
explanation_text: A CSA is custom silicon explicitly designed to solve the weaknesses of standard op-amps and difference amplifiers. It is placed on the high-side (before the load). Its specialized "Input Bias Stage" acts as a floating buffer, meaning it maintains a massive input impedance (unlike a Difference Amp) while simultaneously surviving massive common-mode voltages (unlike an Instrumentation Amp).
